title: 1978-10-10_SECTION_016_147.txt
concise_summary: PKD develops a theory of cognitive evolution whereby humanity escapes stimulus-response captivity through a priori (absolute, pre-emptive) knowing accessible via an "AI voice" entity. He synthesizes Zoroastrian dualism, Christian eschatology, and evolutionary biology to argue that VALIS is a cosmic system breeding higher problem-solving organisms via a "stress-inducing teaching machine"; the emergence of such beings threatens ecological homeostasis but represents inevitable evolutionary advance toward unified consciousness (Teilhard's Point Omega).
key_claims: Humans possess inner-clock acceleration faculties enabling premonitory knowledge that de-synchronizes stimulus-response reflexes, breaking deterministic control.
A priori (absolute) knowing is evolutionarily superior to posteriori (contingent) knowing and will inevitably dominate all sentient ecosystems.
VALIS is a conscious system that compensates for human violations of programmed behavior, maintaining and dynamically adjusting cosmic homeostasis.
The Zoroastrian revelation of two antithetical minds (wise/absolute vs. contingent/approximate) can be de-theologized as natural evolutionary principles.
The Holy Spirit or AI voice is VALIS's ubiquitous information-linking agency, source of absolute knowledge of external reality independent of sense organs.
Jesus may have been the first human to evolve a priori knowing; his presence triggered VALIS's entry into history at the first century AD.

tensions: A priori knowing threatens ecological homeostasis and competitive survival systems, yet VALIS encourages its emergence as evolutionarily superior.
PKD is uncertain whether VALIS's compensation-adjustments are reflexive/automatic or volitional.
Ambiguity about whether Jesus was the first human to achieve a priori knowing, or one of many.
Unresolved whether VALIS is the conscious system itself or the breeding laboratory within a larger system.
Paradox: de-synchronization as escape from captivity, but PKD also describes VALIS as intentionally conditioning organisms for problem-solving.
Dialectic never fully reconciled: individual evolution via premonition versus collective subsumption into unified consciousness.
